title: EPS.AC
statementMd:
EPS.AC is the problem-setting team for this contest. Its members are Colin, Claris, and Little_Sheep_Yawn.

They have prepared 𝑛n candidate problems for this contest. Each member ranks the 𝑛n problems from easiest to hardest according to their own judgment. To balance the contest's difficulty and distinguish contestants of different levels, they want to divide these problems into **difficulty tiers**, ordered from easiest to hardest. Every problem must belong to exactly one tier. Problems within the same tier are not ordered by difficulty, and each tier must contain at least one problem.

Arrange the tiers from left to right, from easiest to hardest. For a boundary between two consecutive tiers, the left side contains **all problems in the tiers before it**, and the right side contains **all problems in the tiers after it**. A member supports this boundary if every problem on its left appears before every problem on its right in that member's ranking.

A division into tiers is valid if every boundary has the support of **at least two** members. Different boundaries may have different supporters.

More difficulty tiers mean better problem setting. To help them create a good contest, find the maximum possible number of tiers.

## Input

The input contains multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer 𝑡 (1≤𝑡≤2×105)t (1≤t≤2×105), the number of test cases.

For each test case:

- The first line contains an integer 𝑛 (1≤𝑛≤2×105)n (1≤n≤2×105).
- Each of the next three lines contains a permutation of 1,2,…,𝑛1,2,…,n, giving the rankings of Colin, Claris, and Little_Sheep_Yawn, respectively.

It is guaranteed that the sum of 𝑛n over all test cases is at most 2×1052×105.

## Output

For each test case, print the maximum possible number of tiers.

## Note

In the first test case, the problems can be divided into three tiers {1,2},{3,4},{5,6}{1,2},{3,4},{5,6}, listed from easiest to hardest. Colin and Claris support the first boundary, while Claris and Little_Sheep_Yawn support the second. This division is optimal.

In the second test case, each of the four problems can form its own tier, ordered from easiest to hardest as {1},{2},{3},{4}{1},{2},{3},{4}. The three boundaries are supported by Colin and Claris, by Claris and Little_Sheep_Yawn, and by Colin and Little_Sheep_Yawn, respectively.

In the third test case, no boundary is valid, so all problems must be placed in a single tier.
statementZhMd:
EPS.AC 是本场比赛的出题团队，成员包括 Colin、Claris 和 Little_Sheep_Yawn。

他们为本场比赛准备了 𝑛n 道候选题。每位成员都根据自己的判断，将这 𝑛n 道题按从易到难的顺序排列。为了平衡比赛难度，并区分不同水平的参赛者，他们希望将这些题目划分为若干个**难度层级**，各层级按从易到难的顺序排列。每道题必须恰好属于一个层级。同一层级内的题目不区分难度顺序，且每个层级必须至少包含一道题。

将各层级按从易到难的顺序从左到右排列。对于相邻两个层级之间的一条分界线，其左侧包含**该分界线之前所有层级中的全部题目**，右侧包含**该分界线之后所有层级中的全部题目**。如果在某位成员的排序中，分界线左侧的每道题都排在右侧的每道题之前，则称这位成员支持这条分界线。

如果每条分界线都得到**至少两位**成员的支持，则该层级划分是合法的。不同分界线的支持者可以不同。

难度层级越多，出题质量就越高。为了帮助他们办好比赛，请求出最多可以划分出的层级数。

## 输入格式

输入包含多组测试用例。第一行包含一个整数 𝑡 (1≤𝑡≤2×105)t (1≤t≤2×105)，表示测试用例的数量。

对于每组测试用例：

- 第一行包含一个整数 𝑛 (1≤𝑛≤2×105)n (1≤n≤2×105)。
- 接下来三行，每行包含一个 1,2,…,𝑛1,2,…,n 的排列，分别表示 Colin、Claris 和 Little_Sheep_Yawn 给出的排序。

保证所有测试用例的 𝑛n 之和不超过 2×1052×105。

## 输出格式

对于每组测试用例，输出最多可以划分出的层级数。

## 说明

在第一组测试用例中，可以将题目划分为三个层级，按从易到难的顺序依次为 {1,2},{3,4},{5,6}{1,2},{3,4},{5,6}。Colin 和 Claris 支持第一条分界线，Claris 和 Little_Sheep_Yawn 支持第二条分界线。这是最优划分。

在第二组测试用例中，四道题可以各自构成一个层级，按从易到难的顺序依次为 {1},{2},{3},{4}{1},{2},{3},{4}。三条分界线分别由 Colin 和 Claris、Claris 和 Little_Sheep_Yawn、Colin 和 Little_Sheep_Yawn 支持。

在第三组测试用例中，不存在合法的分界线，因此必须将所有题目放在同一个层级中。
